insights.headline: Gold falls for third straight session to $4,130 as firm dollar and yields weigh; India flips to a gold premium
insights.summary: Spot gold slipped to $4,130.80 on October 20 for a third straight losing session as a firm dollar and elevated Treasury yields kept pressure on bullion ahead of the October 27-28 FOMC meeting. India’s physical market flipped to a premium for the first time in three months — dealers quoted up to $7 an ounce over spot as festive demand improved and import curbs tightened supply. MCX stayed shut Tuesday morning for Dussehra with gold futures settled at Rs 1,47,300 per 10 grams, while gold ETF holdings hit 2026 highs even as prices sag.
points: Spot gold fell to $4,130.80 on Oct 20, a third straight loss, as dollar and yield strength offset fading October Fed-hike odds. (story 1)
India gold flipped to premium: dealers quote up to $7/oz over spot vs $5-6 discounts last week, as imports plunged 45% in August. (story 2)
Gold ETF holdings hit a 2026 peak of 101.3 moz on Oct 8 despite hot CPI/PPI pressure pushing gold briefly under $4,100. (story 3)
MCX morning session shut for Dussehra; futures settled at Rs 1,47,300/10g gold and Rs 2,09,825/kg silver. (story 1)
Around 17 AMCs froze fresh gold-ETF-FoF inflows from Oct 16 on SEBI's nudge; RBI set SGB Series VII redemption at ₹14,614. (stories 6, 7)

trending.title: Fed rate path is the week's master switch
trending.summary: A firm dollar and elevated yields drove gold to a third straight loss near $4,130, while October hike odds keep fading and December stays heavily priced ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting.

trending.title: ETF investors are buying the dip while futures traders sell
trending.summary: Gold ETF holdings hit 2026 highs on persistent inflows even as prices sag — contrasting with ~17 Indian AMCs freezing fresh gold-fund inflows while central banks keep adding (Goldman: 79t in August).

trending.title: India's physical market is tightening into the festival run
trending.summary: Premiums are back after three months as festive buying meets import curbs, and Delhi gold rose Rs 400 to ₹1.5 lakh with demand picking up ahead of Diwali.

trending.title: Silver's make-or-break $55.40
trending.summary: Silver tests the $55.40 support FXEmpire calls the key decision point, with $48.29 below and $60.63 capping rallies; Hindustan Zinc's Q2 silver output rose 20% on firm prices.

items.title: Gold Price Today, October 20: Bullion heads for third straight session of losses as stronger dollar, higher US yields weigh
items.summary: Spot gold fell for a third straight session on October 20, slipping to $4,130.80 as a stronger dollar and elevated Treasury yields weighed on bullion. In India, MCX skipped the morning session for the Dussehra holiday; futures had settled at Rs 1,47,300 per 10 grams and Rs 2,09,825 per kg, with the evening session scheduled from 5 pm.

items.title: India Gold Market Flips to Premium as Demand Improves and Supplies Tighten
items.summary: Gold traded at a premium in India last week for the first time in three months — dealers quoted up to $7 an ounce over domestic spot versus $5–6 discounts the week before. Festive demand improved after early-October prices fell to a near-two-month low of ₹1,45,538 per 10 grams, while supply tightened as imports plunged 45% in August and slipped again in September after the May duty hike to 15%.

items.title: Gold and silver prices pressured by hot inflation, but gold ETF holdings buck trend to hit 2026 highs
items.summary: Gold and silver came under renewed pressure after elevated US CPI and PPI prints, with gold briefly dipping below $4,100 as the September CPI pushed yields and the dollar higher, Heraeus analysts say. But ETF demand diverged: Bloomberg-tracked holdings hit a 2026 peak of 101.3 million ounces on October 8, up 5.3% from the July low. Fading October 28 hike odds helped gold recover $4,100 support.

items.title: Gold price reverses gains as investors weigh Fed rate path
items.summary: Spot gold slipped about 0.5% to near $4,144 in New York trading on Monday, erasing an earlier 0.6% gain, as investors weighed the Fed's rate path ahead of the October 27-28 FOMC meeting. Warsh's remarks have cut October hike odds to ~15%, though December stays heavily priced. Forex.com's Fawad Razaqzada told Reuters a hawkish Fed message could bring further short-term weakness.

items.title: Gold, silver rise on MCX as Fed rate hike odds drop below 20%
items.summary: MCX December gold futures traded at ₹1,48,379 per 10 grams, up 0.31%, and December silver at ₹2,12,013 per kg, up 0.39%, in early trade on October 19, tracking firm COMEX cues after Warsh's Bangkok remarks pushed October hike odds below 20%. Experts said a firmer rupee is capping domestic gains; resistance for MCX gold sits at ₹1,48,600.

items.title: Did Mutual Funds Stop Gold Investments? What Investors Need to Know
items.summary: ET explains the October 16 freeze on fresh investments into gold ETF fund-of-funds by around 17 fund houses, after a SEBI nudge via AMFI ahead of the festive season. New lump-sum, SIP and STP registrations are paused; existing SIPs and redemptions continue, and gold ETFs still trade on exchanges. The curbs aim to cool paper-gold inflows that feed bullion imports and rupee pressure.

items.title: RBI sets SGB 2020-21 Series VII redemption at Rs 14,614 for October 19
items.summary: The RBI has fixed October 19, 2026 as the premature redemption date for Sovereign Gold Bond 2020-21 Series VII at Rs 14,614 per gram, based on IBJA's average closing prices of October 14-16. Online subscribers gain 192.22% and offline buyers 189.33% in capital gains, alongside 2.5% annual interest; holders must route requests through their receiving offices within the notification window.

items.title: Gold price to touch ₹1.60 lakh by Dec 2026 end? Time to buy? What experts say to earn money from yellow metal deals
items.summary: Mint quotes market expert Anuj Gupta and PACE 360's Amit Goel projecting gold at ₹1.60 lakh per 10 gm in India and $4,600 an ounce globally by end-December 2026. Both expect the Fed to hold rates on October 27-28 — about 85% priced, per CME FedWatch — which they say could push gold decisively past ₹1.50 lakh. MCX December futures are near ₹1.48 lakh, up 26.5% since Dussehra 2025.

items.title: Goldman Sachs estimates central banks bought 79 tonnes of gold in August, led by China
items.summary: Goldman Sachs estimates central banks bought 79 tonnes of gold in August — over 4x the pre-2022 monthly average of 17 tonnes and up from 44t in July — calling official demand a structural support for gold. China was the largest buyer at ~25t, above the PBOC's reported ~20t. The bank builds its gauge from trade and flow data, not disclosures, and says the numbers can be revised.

items.title: Silver (XAG/USD) Price Forecast: $55.40 Support Puts Bearish Trend at a Crossroads
items.summary: FXEmpire's technical analysis says silver is testing critical support at $55.40, with the next move deciding whether the bearish trend resumes or a countertrend recovery develops. A breakdown could expose $48.29 (78.6% Fibonacci retracement); resistance sits at the 20-day average near $60.63 and the 50-day near $63.80. The bounce so far is muted, leaving any recovery unconfirmed.

items.title: Gold climbs Rs 400 to Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 gm as festive buying elevates demand
items.summary: Delhi gold rose Rs 400 to Rs 1,50,300 per 10 grams, inclusive of taxes, on Monday as festive demand picked up ahead of Dussehra; silver held steady at Rs 2.15 lakh per kg. HDFC Securities' Saumil Gandhi said domestic gold traded at a premium last week for the first time in three months and expects retail demand to build toward Diwali. Bullion markets shut Tuesday for Dussehra.

items.title: Hindustan Zinc Q2 profit more than doubles on higher metal prices; silver output up 20%
items.summary: Hindustan Zinc's consolidated net profit more than doubled to Rs 6,412 crore in Q2 FY27 as higher metal prices and record output lifted revenue 76.5% to Rs 15,093 crore, margin widening to 42%. Silver production rose 20% to 173 tonnes and silver sales revenue more than doubled, driving about 45% of profitability; Jefferies said firmer silver prices improved the profit outlook.

items.title: IBJA's Surendra Mehta sees gold rallying 10-12% to $4,700 by November 30
items.summary: IBJA national secretary Surendra Mehta told ET Now Swadesh he expects gold to rally 10-12% by November 30, potentially reaching $4,700 an ounce, as bond yields ease below 5.1% and crude stabilises near $105. He put the downside at 4-5% (a move toward $3,850 not ruled out) and said India's festive season could support prices, barring fresh geopolitical escalation.

items.title: Gold and silver head for volatile week amid crude oil spike, West Asia worries
items.summary: PTI reports MCX December gold fell Rs 3,581 (-2.4%) last week to Rs 1.47 lakh/10g, and silver Rs 14,568 (-6.4%) to Rs 2.11 lakh/kg. The rupee's jump to 94.8 from ~96.8 in five sessions on RBI intervention cut import costs, dragging domestic prices down ~5x the global fall. Analysts expect a capped, choppy week: Brent near $110, West Asia tensions, and Tuesday's Dussehra morning closure.
